extracted.intended_audience: fiction writers / prose authors (especially those writing contemporary short fiction and novels)
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance for fiction writers on revising prose that reads like film by emphasizing prose-specific strengths (interiority, temporal control, subjective POV) and removing filmic, camera-like description.

rubrics_metrics.name: TV brain (core problem)
rubrics_metrics.description: Contemporary fiction often exhibits 'TV brain' — authors mentally visualizing scenes like film and translating that directly to prose, abandoning the unique strengths of written narrative.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recognize when you're transcribing a mental video instead of writing with the tools of prose. The symptom is prose that reads like a camera log or shot list rather than as mediated human perception and consciousness.

rubrics_metrics.name: Eliminate unnecessary movement description
rubrics_metrics.description: Skip banal, procedural action descriptions unless they serve characterization or theme.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid cataloging every gesture (anti-pattern: listing each small movement). A single brief line such as 'She got a glass of water' can suffice; only expand on action when the movement reveals character, advances theme, or has emotional/plot significance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Develop robust interiority
rubrics_metrics.description: Use prose's prime advantage: direct access to character interiority and consciousness.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Move beyond dialogue and surface action that merely repeats itself. Show genuine internal conflict, thoughts, feelings, perceptions, and complexity — let inner life do work that film would otherwise imply visually.

rubrics_metrics.name: Recalibrate POV as subjective
rubrics_metrics.description: Make point-of-view explicitly subjective: details should reflect what characters would realistically notice and be colored by their perspective.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid neutral, camera-like description. Filter sensory detail, significance, and interpretation through the character's attention, emotions, knowledge, and biases so scenes register as lived experience rather than objective snapshots.

rubrics_metrics.name: Embrace temporal flexibility
rubrics_metrics.description: Exploit prose's complete control over time: you can compress centuries or expand seconds.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use summarization, compression, and expansion strategically rather than defaulting to real-time scene playing. Choose which moments to linger on and which to summarize to shape pacing and emphasis.

rubrics_metrics.name: Lean into prose-specific strengths
rubrics_metrics.description: Favor what prose does best: interiority, temporal manipulation, and subjective filtering rather than filmic visual immediacy.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When revising, intentionally prioritize interior access, selective temporal focus, and the character's subjective filter. Ask whether each sentence exploits these strengths—or instead mimics what a camera could show.

rubrics_metrics.name: Do not rely on visual-media affordances
rubrics_metrics.description: Recognize visual media advantages (faces/bodies are compelling; small movements register instantly) and avoid assuming prose will convey those effects the same way.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If a scene depends on the instantaneous visual power of a face or minute physical movement, rework it so the emotion or information is present in interior thought, focused detail, or narrative emphasis; don't expect readers to 'see' a filmic moment simply because you described it.

rubrics_metrics.name: Key principle: use the medium, don't mimic another
rubrics_metrics.description: Lean into what your medium does best. Prose is not film; do not write fiction as if describing a video playing in your mind.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use this as an overarching revision test: whenever prose feels cinematic rather than literary, ask how you can translate the moment into interior perception, selective detail, or temporal shaping appropriate to prose.
